experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: frecip.s $f0, $f0; frecip.s $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'frecip.s $f0, $f0; frecip.s $f0, $f0; movfr2gr.s $r4, $f0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; movgr2fr.w $f0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency: 8 cycles for 0/Inf/NaN; 10 for 1 and powers of two; 16 for 3, 5, 7, 10, 1/3 and 1/5; 15 for max; 17 for maxsub. Measured with an integer-bit reset chain; 5 cycles of helper latency are subtracted. The sample experiment uses 1.0.

throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput: CPI 4.5 for special values; 5.5 for powers of two; 8.5 for general inputs; 8.0 for max; 9.0 for maxsub. Throughput is initiation-interval bound.

notes: Latency model, fitted and validated on this core with a two-copy chain (the stored experiment runs the operation twice, subtracts the 6-cycle closure and divides by 2). Classes: 8 cycles for special operands (0, Inf, NaN), 10 cycles for the exact / power-of-two path (the stored sample uses 1.0), 17 cycles for a general operand. For 32-bit lanes the vector latency equals 2 x the scalar latency - 5, because the 32-bit lanes make two passes over the 64-bit datapath and share the setup/rounding. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers exactly and run in parallel, only the slowest lane matters.
